No.406/DG/EPA/2025 
GOVERNMENT OF THE PUNJAB 
ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTIONAL AGENCY 
NATIONAL HOCKEY STADIUM FEROZEPUR ROAD, LAHORE 
 
                               Dated: 21.11.2025 
  
PUBLIC ADVISORY  
 
Subject: 
ADVICE 
FOR 
GENERAL 
PUBLIC 
U/S 
6(1)(o) 
OF 
THE 
PUNJAB                  
ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION ACT, 1997 
 
 
 
  WHEREAS, Govt. of Punjab is striving hard to combat the devastating 
impacts of prevailing smog season. Pre-emptive measures against all the sources of air 
pollution have already started by EPA as well as other concerned departments; 
2. 
 
AND WHEREAS, as per Section 2(xxxiii) of  the  Punjab Environmental 
Protection Act 1997, pollution means the contamination of air, land or water by the discharge 
or emission of effluents or wastes or air pollutants or noise or other matter which either directly 
or indirectly or in combination with other discharges or substances alters unfavorably the 
chemical, physical, biological, radiation, thermal or radiological or aesthetic properties of the 
air, land or water or which may, or is likely to make the air, land or water unclean, noxious or 
impure or injurious, disagreeable or detrimental to the health, safety, welfare or property of 
persons or harmful to biodiversity. 
3.  
 
AND WHEREAS various human activities, including vehicular emissions, 
reliance on private transport, traditional cooking fuels, deforestation, and open burning, 
significantly contribute to air pollution and environmental degradation. Idling vehicles, 
excessive fuel consumption, and burning waste and crop residues release harmful pollutants, 
worsening air quality and climate change. Citizens play a vital role in reducing emissions by 
adopting sustainable practices. A collective effort towards these actions is essential for a 
cleaner, healthier, and more sustainable environment.  
4. 
        AND WHEREAS, owing to the sustained cooperation of the general public, 
including adherence to precautionary measures and reduction in non-essential vehicular 
movement, the Government has recorded a notable improvement in the smog situation during 
the current season; such collective public compliance remains crucial for maintaining these 
gains and further mitigating pollution across the province; 
 


[[PAGE 2]]
5. 
 
AND WHEREAS, Section 6(1) (o) of the ibid Act empowers EPA to provide 
information and guidance to the public on environmental matters; 
6.  
 
NOW, THEREFORE, I, Dr. Imran Hamid Sheikh, PAS, Director General, 
Environmental Protection Agency, Punjab in exercise of the powers conferred upon me U/S 
6(1)(o) of the Punjab Environmental Protection Act 1997, do hereby advise the general public 
during the weekend i.e. Saturday and Sunday that they must: 
i. 
All residents are advised to remain indoors and avoid unnecessary outdoor 
movement, especially during peak smog hours.  
ii. 
Wear protective masks and seek medical attention in case of respiratory 
distress, coughing, eye irritation, or chest discomfort. 
iii. 
Keep windows and doors closed during high smog periods. 
iv. 
Seek immediate medical attention if experiencing breathing difficulties, 
coughing, or irritation in eyes or throat 
v. 
Minimize the use of private vehicles, including cars and motorbikes, to 
reduce emissions. Only essential travel should be undertaken. 
vi. 
Prefer carpooling and mass transit to reduce traffic congestion and 
emissions 
vii. 
Use eco-friendly transport options like bicycles and electric vehicles where 
possible. 
viii. 
Turn off vehicle engines while idling at red lights, parking areas, and 
congested roads. 
ix. 
Avoid burning garbage, leaves, and crop residues to reduce air pollution 
and smog formation. 
 
 
 
      DR. IMRAN HAMID SHEIKH (PAS) 
       Director General  
   Environmental Protection Agency          
Punjab
